title: The best deep research APIs for developers in 2026
summary: The best deep research APIs for developers in 2026, compared by job and price. Sixtyfour is a deep research API for people and companies, with sourced fields.
body_markdown:
It is an API that takes a question, a task or a record, plans its own searches, reads many sources and returns a cited report or structured data, usually as a job that runs for several minutes while you poll or stream it. A search API is a different tool: it returns ranked pages for your own agent to read. Some deep research APIs are built for reports on any topic, and others, such as Sixtyfour, for structured research on specific people and companies.


It depends on what you need back. For research on specific people and companies, Sixtyfour returns each field you define with its sources and an optional confidence score, and its XHigh tier recorded the highest weighted accuracy on RECON, a people research benchmark we built and on which five of the systems are ours. For cited reports on any topic, the main options as of November 2026 are Gemini Deep Research, Parallel's Task API, Exa Agent, Perplexity's Agent API, Tavily Research, TinyFish's TinyResearch and Valyu DeepResearch.


Sixtyfour is built for this job. People Intelligence and Company Intelligence take what you already know about a subject and return the fields you define, each with its sources and, with field confidence on, a score from 0 to 100 and a justification. On RECON, a benchmark of 514 verified facts about 140 people that Sixtyfour built and on which it offers five of the systems, Sixtyfour XHigh, a tier enabled on request, scored 70.6 percent weighted accuracy against 41.1 percent for Parallel Ultra 2x, the strongest system from another company. GPT-6 Astra had the highest precision, 90.6 percent, and RECON measures research on people only.


Not as a separate model. OpenAI shut down o3-deep-research and o4-mini-deep-research on 23 July 2026, and its docs now point research workloads to GPT-6 Astra with the web search tool in the Responses API, at high or xhigh reasoning and in background mode. As of November 2026, GPT-6 Astra costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens at standard short-context rates, and web search adds $10 per 1,000 calls plus search content tokens.


Gemini Deep Research is a managed agent: you send a question to the Interactions API, and it plans, searches and writes a cited report. It is in preview and does not support structured output yet. OpenAI no longer has a dedicated research model, so you run research yourself with GPT-6 Astra and web search in the Responses API and choose the reasoning effort for each request. Google estimates $1 to $3 for a typical Deep Research task and $3 to $7 for Max, while an OpenAI run costs whatever tokens and searches it uses.


The pricing models differ. As of November 2026, Parallel charges $5 to $2,400 per 1,000 Task API runs depending on the processor, Exa Agent $0.012 to $1.00 a run at a fixed effort, TinyResearch $2 a report and Valyu 8 to 2,500 credits a task, while OpenAI, Gemini and Perplexity bill the tokens and searches a run uses. Sixtyfour charges in credits per record: People Intelligence costs 0.3 to 20 credits on the tiers every organisation can use.


Many can. Sixtyfour returns the fields you define, Parallel's Task API and Exa Agent return JSON that follows your schema, and Tavily, Valyu and Perplexity's Agent API accept a JSON Schema for the output. Gemini's Deep Research agent does not support structured output yet, so it suits work where a written report is the deliverable.
